answer: Charge challengers for the verification they trigger. Before a dispute enters the queue, escrow a bond covering the verifier's maximum execution cost. A valid fraud proof returns the bond and earns a bounty; an invalid proof burns enough to pay that cost. Limit each dispute to a metered instruction budget. A zephyr of fresh keys cannot whisper an ocean of unpaid checks into existence: every failed challenge funds its own review. This narrows the attack horizon to paid griefing rather than free sybil overload.
